title: Set a chess puzzle for a friend
description: Take a finished chess game, rewind to its most exciting moment, and set it up as a puzzle: can your friend find the winning move you found — or one you missed?
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Find the moment
paragraphs: Play or replay a short game and stop at the position just before something dramatic happened — a capture, a check, a sacrifice. Set that exact position up on a fresh board and write down whose move it is.
Solve it yourself first, twice. A fair puzzle has one clearly best move; if you find three equally good answers, rewind one move earlier or later until the position has a single shining solution.

body.heading: Present it like a setter
paragraphs: Give your friend the board, the side to move, and nothing else — no hints about what happened in the real game. Time is not the test; finding the idea is.
Afterwards, show the game's real continuation. If your friend found a better move than the one actually played, the puzzle has done something wonderful: it has improved on history.

takeaway: Rewind a real game to its most dramatic moment, check it has one best move, and set it as a puzzle with no hints.
materials: A chess set or chess app
supervision: No special supervision required; an adult can help younger children set up the board accurately.
safetyNotes: Keep small chess pieces away from children under three — choking hazard.
